main_text.head: METAPHYSICÆ LIBER PRIMUS.
CAPUT I.
De natura Metaphysicæ,
THEOREMATA.
main_text.p: 1 METAPHYSICA est ars contemplativa, quæ tractat de omni intelligibili, quatenus ab homine naturali rationis lumi-ne sine ullo materia conceptu est intelligibile.Def. M[?]
2 Eius partes sunt duæ; una universalis, altera particularis.Par.[?]
main_text.head: IN CAPUT PRIMUM.
PROBLEMA I.
main_text.p: TANTVS hactenus ubiq; locorum & contemptus fuit nobilissimæ hu-plinæ[?], quæ METAPHYSICA nuncupatur, ut multi non tantum illam ignoraverint; verum etiam utrum omnino sit talis aliqua disciplina, dubitaverint. Quoniam vero nemini aditus patet ad adyta arcana Metaphysicæ, nisi certus omnino sit & persuasus in animo suo, illam dari: operæ pretium me facturum puto, si in vestibulo huius artis ante omnia eius existentiam probem. Suntigitur sequentia argumenta observanda:

1 Si dantur principia & attributa generalia ac commu-nia, quibus omnia entia, quæ in aliis disciplinis traduntur, naturæ cognatione inter se conveniunt, datur etiam ars aliqua generalis, quæ hæc omnia consideret & explicet. Naturalis enim sciendi appetitus qui est in homini-bus, præsertim Philosophiæ studio addictis, nihil incogni-tum relinquit: sed eo usque in singularum rerum conside-ratione progreditur, donec ad ultima metam pervenias, ultra quam nihil amplius contemplandum inveniatur ac restet. Jam autem nemo sanæ mentis homo negare potest,Metaphysicæ dari, Ratio I.

page.notes: Printed text in the right margin is cut at the edge: the theses' notes read "Def. M" and "Par." and are uncertain. The initial T is a woodcut letter, joined to "ANTVS". "hu-plinæ" at the line end is doubtful: the printed reading may be a misprint, so the word is marked [?]. "pervenias" is read as printed but is uncertain. The head mark at the top is a faint numeral, read as I with [?]. No catchword is visible at the foot.
